qt: to the Commission Ioan-Rareş Bogdan (PPE) Subject:

The Commission has unveiled the Affordable Housing Act and claims it will help councils to tackle the surge in housing prices and rents in major urban and tourist centres. Commendable though this initiative is, I feel it could turn the right to housing into a paper chase. It reduces the solution of building new homes to nothing more than an unfunded recommendation, foists a strict Brussels-mandated filter onto local authorities under the pretext of the single market, and blocks swift interventions with conditions that help the big short-term rental platforms. 1.

How does the Commission justify the requirement for councils to provide statistical evidence of three consecutive years of a housing crisis before they can limit short-term rentals, leaving the public defenceless against immediate speculation?

How does this rigid framework square with the principle of subsidiarity, given that it leaves local authorities open to commercial litigation if they step in to relieve a squeeze on the housing market?
How does the Commission respond to allegations on social media that it is protecting the big rental platforms?
